findings.area: documentation accuracy - architecture section 8 / ADR-018 Consequences failure blast-radius bound
findings.summary: The comparative phrase 'the failure blast radius is wider than the pre-11.2 per-item library read' is not strictly demonstrated; the concrete bound it describes is accurate.
findings.detail: Architecture section 8 (working tree) and ADR-018 Consequences correctly record the shipped bound: a library read failure during a population caches nothing, returns the bounded failure, and each work item that waited on the per-connection gate re-checks the empty cache and re-attempts the population. That part matches RadarrMetadataReader.PopulateAsync (lines 176-180) and SonarrMetadataReader.PopulateAsync (lines 213-217). The closing comparative clause, however, is not quantified: pre-11.2 each work item already performed its own library read and failed independently, and post-11.2 each work item also re-attempts independently, so the failure count is not demonstrably wider. The one concrete way the impact widens is latency/queue serialization (same-connection readers block on the population gate behind a slow/failing library read), which the sentence does not name. The integration test for this path (RadarrLibraryReadFailureOnACacheMiss...) uses a single work item, so it does not exercise a multi-item window. The claim is conservative (it overstates rather than understates risk), so it is not an overclaim and does not affect acceptance.
evidence: docs/architecture.md section 8 (git diff hunk around line 696: 'so the failure blast radius is wider than the pre-11.2 per-item library read')
docs/decisions.md ADR-018 Consequences: 'A library read failure during a population caches nothing and returns the bounded failure...'
findings.recommended_action: Optional rewording only: state the concrete bound (a failed population leaves the connection window unpopulated and same-connection readers serialize behind the population gate) without the unquantified 'wider than pre-11.2' comparison. Not required for acceptance.

findings.area: documentation consistency - ADR-018 clause 5 vs ADR-018 Consequences
findings.summary: ADR-018 Decision clause 5 still reads 'on provider failure the existing bounded last-known-good semantics apply' while the updated Consequences states a library read failure caches nothing; the two are only reconciled by reading 'existing semantics' as the per-item metadata state.
findings.detail: Task 11.4 correctly corrected the shipped-behavior sentences in architecture sections 8 and 12, data-model section 6, and the ArrInventoryCache* XML docs, and added ADR-018 Consequences clauses stating that failure-driven *inventory* last-known-good retention is not realized. ADR-018 clause 5 itself is left unchanged ('on provider failure the existing bounded last-known-good semantics apply'). A reader can reconcile this only by interpreting 'the existing ... semantics' as the pre-existing per-item MetadataStateEntry last-known-good retention, which the integration test does confirm (MetadataReconciliationProcessor.KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale). The worker did not rewrite a historical decision clause, which is the correct treatment; no acceptance criterion requires changing the clause. This overlaps the parallel documentation-maintainer finding D-11.4-3 (status: recorded). Not a correctness defect in the shipped behavior or the tests.
findings.recommended_action: No change required. Optionally add one clause/note clarifying that the ADR-018 clause-5 'existing bounded last-known-good semantics' is realized by the per-item metadata state, not by the inventory cache.
